args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, it failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. We rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before deploying it again, and check why the release went to production when the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

**What was wrong:** the latest deploy, v2.3.1, was running in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). It was failing health checks with an error rate of 18%.

**Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is down to 0.2%.

**Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the current status. It also lists two next steps:
- Find out what broke in v2.3.1 before deploying it again.
- Find out why v2.3.1 reached production when its test build (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.
